tier_reason: No valid speed number exists. The current README has none and speedtest/src/runner.rs commits no results. Older README revisions (up to v0.6.11, e.g. commit 927a4fa) had a Lanczos3 table against fast_image_resize, but it was measured on filter code that built Lanczos3 kernels at half the correct support, so pic-scale did about half the convolution work of the baseline. The table was deleted in the same commit that fixed this (30b40e5, v0.6.12), so it cannot support a tier above D.

corrections.claimed_speedup: none valid. The current README has no numbers. README revisions up to v0.6.11 (e.g. commit 927a4fa, 2025-04-30) had a Performance table for downscaling a 4928x3279 image 4x with Lanczos3: RGB pic-scale 10.47 (AVX2) / 6.97 (NEON) against fast_image_resize 15.62 / 21.74; RGBA without premultiplication 11.13 / 7.76 against 20.17 / 25.92, Apple Accelerate 9.98 (NEON); units unstated. Those runs used the pre-0.6.12 kernel-size code (src/scaler.rs: filter_base_size = min_kernel_size, so a Lanczos3 window of radius 1.5 x scale instead of 3 x scale), i.e. pic-scale used roughly half the taps of fast_image_resize. The section was removed in commit 30b40e5 ('Filter generation fix', v0.6.12, 2025-10-16), which doubled the kernel size.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 41 stars, 1 fork; crate pic-scale 0.7.12 with about 1.45 million crates.io downloads (1.33 million recent); 5 crates.io dependents (hayro, media-core, oximg, spectrograph, zenresize; some may be dev-dependencies)
corrections.caveats: The current README, repo page and speedtest folder (src and Cargo.toml only) carry no results. Current harness bug confirmed: in speedtest/src/runner.rs, runner_rgba_fir allocates the fast_image_resize destination with Image::new(target_size.width, target_size.width, ...), i.e. width x width. make_sizes produces proportional non-square targets (w/2 x h/2 and so on for the 4928x3279 PNG), so fast_image_resize renders a taller output than pic-scale, which would flatter pic-scale in any chart. pic-scale reuses a precomputed plan, scratch and destination buffers, while fast_image_resize rebuilds its options per call; fast_image_resize runs single-threaded. Historical numbers are invalid for comparison: the README Performance table (present up to v0.6.11, e.g. commit 927a4fa; Apple M3 Pro for NEON, an unnamed 'Premium Intel CPU Optimized 4 vCPU Digital Ocean instance' for AVX2; criterion benches in app/benches/resize_rgb and resize_rgba, both libraries single-threaded, rustc version and flags not given) was measured when pic-scale's src/scaler.rs set the Lanczos3 kernel size to round(3 x scale) with radius 1.5 x scale, half the support of a correct Lanczos3 window, so pic-scale computed a truncated filter with about half the taps of fast_image_resize. Commit 30b40e5 ('Filter generation fix', v0.6.12, 2025-10-16) doubled the kernel size (src/math/weights.rs) and deleted the Performance section in the same change. The benchmarked pic-scale rows also ran WorkloadStrategy::PreferSpeed (the default, documented as 'prefers speed to quality'). imazen/zenresize ships a paired_bench harness comparing pic-scale 0.7 with fast_image_resize 6 single-threaded but commits no cross-library results. Same author as libblur, sparkyuv, moxcms and yuvutils-rs.

notes: Stays D. The record said there were no numbers, but older README revisions had a pic-scale vs fast_image_resize table. It was measured on a Lanczos3 kernel truncated to half width, a bug fixed in v0.6.12 by the same commit that deleted the table. Notable by usage (about 1.45 million crates.io downloads), so keep.

tier_reason: No numbers against Little CMS or any other library. bench.c (on the mirror branch) times skcms_Transform alone on 255-pixel batches and says it is 'mostly to run in a profiler'. The READMEs on both branches make no speed claim, and one WebSearch query found nothing numeric.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 4 stars, 3 forks on the GitHub mirror (read-only mirror of skia.googlesource.com/skcms; latest tag 2025_09_16); used by Skia and Chromium, and an optional colour backend of libjxl (per search snippets and the libjxl enrichment)
corrections.caveats: No numeric comparison against Little CMS was found. The main-branch README only describes the mirror; the mirror-branch README covers building only. bench.c (raw.githubusercontent.com/google/skcms/mirror/bench.c; it is absent from main) times skcms alone (default sRGB to Display P3, -n 100000 iterations) and prints no lcms2 figure. imazen/cms-bench has a harness comparing moxcms, lcms2, skcms and ArgyllCMS but commits no results. skia.googlesource.com and the Chromium review thread 'Enable skcms in Skia' (groups.google.com) are blocked here, so a speed claim there could not be checked. Little CMS fast_float is already on the list. The mirror's last commit is 2025-09-16 ('Disable must_tail on GCC when compiling for RISC-V'), 12.6 months before 2026-10-04, so it reads as stale by the 12-month rule. Upstream on skia.googlesource.com may be newer if the mirror sync stopped; this could not be checked.

notes: Stays D, confirmed. Notable as Skia and Chromium's colour-management library despite 4 mirror stars, so keep. Maintenance is judged from the mirror only.

tier_reason: These are first-party go test -bench results in the README, produced by the public scanx_benchmark_test.go, which runs ImgSpanner and LinkListSpanner against scanFT and x/image/vector (via rasterx ScannerGV) on the same icon set. Every quoted ns/op figure matches the README. The CPU model, Go version and flags are not given, so the evidence is C.

corrections.license: FTL OR GPL-2.0-or-later on scan.go only (header inherited from freetype-go, which points to a LICENSE file the repo does not have); span.go and the repo carry no license
corrections.caveats: Baselines are Go scanners: scanFT (the author's own port of the freetype-go antialiaser) and x/image/vector through rasterx ScannerGV. There is no Skia, Cairo or Blend2D comparison and no cross-language comparison. scanx's scan.go is the same freetype-go area/coverage antialiaser adapted to a Spanner interface, so the gain over scanFT comes from the span write path (span.go), not from a new rasterisation algorithm. The CPU model and Go version are missing. At 5x and 15x most rows ran b.N of 1 to 5 times (single-shot). Times include oksvg path traversal and Dasher stroking, and LinkListSpanner timings include DrawToImage. Per the rasterx README, ScannerGV draws through x/image/vector Draw with the path as an alpha mask and 'can be faster for smaller and more complex images'. The harness gives it the full image bounds, which probably explains the 74x gap (not profiled), so the GV figure does not represent x/image/vector on small paths. The README warns 'Scanx is beta software. There are known bugs being worked on. Please use scanFT or scanGV unless you want to test each svg file', and it reports pixel differences from scanFT of up to 4 per pixel (randspot.svg). LinkListSpanner does not support gradients and is slow on line-heavy files (rl.svg). Licence: there is no LICENSE or COPYING file (raw LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt and COPYING all return 404; the GitHub page shows no license). scan.go carries the freetype-go header (FreeType License or GPL-2.0-or-later); span.go, which holds ImgSpanner and LinkListSpanner, has no license header, so only scan.go is clearly reusable. The last commit is 2019-03-09.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 2 stars, 0 forks; default rasteriser of tdewolff/canvas (go.mod pins github.com/srwiley/scanx v0.0.0-20190309010443-e94503791388; renderers/rasterizer/rasterizer.go builds on scanx.NewImgSpanner and scanx.NewScanner)

notes: C confirmed and all numbers match the README. Usability corrected from reference to mixed: scan.go keeps the freetype-go FTL/GPL-2.0+ header, while span.go (the fast part) and the repo have no license. The beta and known-bugs warning was added to caveats.
